Based on the survey results, how many students identified chess or basketball as their favorite sport?

On DJ Snake’s engagement day, the total value of all the treats he received was $158,000. Moksi took him and his fiancée to a luxurious hotel for two nights at $4,000 per night. Lil Jon bought them a car, and Wynter presented them with a house worth four times the value of that car. What was the price of the car Lil Jon bought?

Ms. Jones has 50 students in her class. She received thank you cards from some of them, and 1/3 of those cards included a $10 gift card. If the total value of the gift cards was $50, what percentage of her class sent her a thank you card?

Ms. Jones teaches a class. After a school event, 30% of her students sent her thank-you cards. Of those cards, exactly one-third contained a $10 gift card to a bookstore. In total, she received $50 in gift cards. Additionally, 40% of the thank-you cards had stickers on the envelopes, and 2 of the cards (neither of which had a gift card) included $5 coupons that she did not count toward the gift card total. How many students are in her class?

Kimiko is retiling her kitchen and a small pantry. The kitchen floor measures 48 inches by 72 inches, but there is a rectangular floor vent measuring 12 inches by 18 inches that will not be tiled. The pantry measures 24 inches by 36 inches and will be tiled fully. Each tile covers 6 square inches. How many tiles does Kimiko need to buy in total?
Kimiko plans to cover a rectangular kitchen floor measuring 48 inches by 72 inches with square tiles that are 6 inches on each side. How many tiles does she need to buy?

Toby has two rectangles of cloth. The first is 4.0 inches wide and 5.0 inches tall. The second is 3.0 inches wide and 6.0 inches tall. How many more square inches is the area of the first compared to the second?

Toby has two rectangles of cloth. The second is 3 inches wide and 6 inches tall. The first is 4 inches wide, and its area is 2 square inches greater than the area of the second. What is the height of the first rectangle?

Two rectangular pieces of fabric are measured. One is 4 inches by 5 inches, and the other is 3 inches by 6 inches. By how many square inches does the area of the 4-by-5 piece exceed the area of the 3-by-6 piece?

Mitchell is trying to chew as many pieces of gum at once as he can. He has 8.0 packets of gum, There are 7.0 pieces in each. If he chews all the gum except for 2.0 pieces, how many pieces does he chew at once?

Liz's basketball team is down by 20 points at the start of the final quarter. In the first minute, the other team scores 5 more points on a 3-pointer and two free throws. Liz then goes on a shooting spree, sinking 5 free throws, 3 three-pointers, and 4 other jump shots. In addition, she makes 2 layups, and on one of her three-pointers she is fouled and makes the bonus free throw. One of Liz’s teammates also scores a 2-point jumper and later makes two free throws. After those early 5 points, the other team scores 10 more points in the quarter, and no other points are scored. By how many points does Liz’s team lose at the end of the game?

At the start of the fourth quarter, Liz’s team trails by 20 points. In that period, Liz is the only one on her team to score: she makes 5 free throws, sinks 3 three-pointers, and hits 4 regular two-point jumpers. The opposing team scores 10 points in the quarter. What is the final margin by which Liz’s team loses?

Liz's basketball team is down by 20 points in the final quarter of their game. Liz goes on a shooting spree, sinking 5 free throw shots, 3 three-pointers, and 4 other jump shots. The other team only scores 10 points that quarter. How much does Liz's team lose by at the end of the game?

Kris has been suspended for bullying many times. For every instance of bullying, she was suspended for 3.0 days. If she has been suspended for 3.0 times as many days as a typical person has fingers and toes, how many instances of bullying is she responsible for?

Kate saved $27 in March, $13 in April, and $28 in May. In June, she saved twice as much as she did in April. She also received a $24 gift and put half of it into her savings. Then Kate spent $49 on a keyboard, $5 on a mouse, and bought 3 USB drives for $4 each. After that, she returned one of the USB drives for a full refund. How much money does Kate have left?
Kate set aside $27 in March, added $13 in April, and saved another $28 in May. She then bought a keyboard for $49 and a mouse for $5. How much money remains from her savings?

Over the course of a week, Beth bakes 4 batches of cookies, with each batch containing 2 dozen cookies. If she distributes all the cookies evenly among 16 people, how many cookies does each person receive?

Beth is baking for a club meeting. She makes 4 batches of cookies, and each batch yields exactly 2 dozen cookies. Of these, 48 are chocolate chip and the rest are sugar cookies, with 12 of the sugar cookies decorated with sprinkles. She also brings 40 paper plates that end up unused. If only the cookies are shared equally among 16 people at the meeting, how many cookies does each person receive?

At a school fair, a judge measures only the total distance each bottle cap travels through the air (ignoring any rolling after it lands). A steady 5 mph crosswind blows during both throws, and both caps weigh 3 grams. Jenny’s red cap, spinning at 600 rpm, flies 18 feet straight before striking a 12-foot-tall streetlight; after the bounce it travels another one-third of the distance it had already flown. Mark’s blue cap, spinning at 800 rpm, flies 15 feet forward before clipping a window 6 feet above the ground; after the bounce it travels twice as far as it had already flown. If all distances are measured exactly along the flight path, how much farther did Mark’s bottle cap go than Jenny’s?

At the county fair’s petting zoo, Mary is counting only the animals roaming in the main pen. A sign mentions there are 10 chickens in a closed coop and 6 bunnies in the nursery, which she is not including in her tally. In the main pen, she correctly counts all 4 goats and both llamas exactly once. However, she accidentally counts 7 of the sheep twice and forgets to count 3 of the pigs. If her clipboard shows a total of 60 animals for the main pen, how many animals are actually in the pen?

Jackson is clearing out his email inbox after noticing he has a whole lot of emails that he no longer needs and can delete. While he is cleaning his inbox, though, he keeps getting more emails. While he deletes 100/2 emails he gets another 15.0 sent to him. While he deletes 60/3 more he receives 10/2 more emails. After he is done deleting all his old emails he has just the new emails left, including 30/3 more that were sent to him. How many emails are there in Jackson's inbox now?

Adonis is playing a prank on his dad by replacing his shampoo with hot sauce. Every day, after his dad showers, Adonis replaces the shampoo with 3/4 of an ounce of hot sauce. He knows his dad uses 1 1/2 oz of shampoo a day from a new 12 oz bottle that no one else uses. After 6 days, what percentage of the liquid in the bottle is hot sauce?

Adonis is playing a prank on his dad by swapping in hot sauce. His dad uses exactly 1 oz per day from a new 10 oz shampoo bottle that no one else uses. After each shower, Adonis adds the same fixed amount of hot sauce to the bottle. After 4 days, 25% of the liquid in the bottle is hot sauce. How many ounces of hot sauce is Adonis adding each day?

Adonis decides to prank his dad using a new 10 oz shampoo bottle that only his dad uses. The bottle has a pump that dispenses 0.25 oz per press, and his dad always uses 4 pumps per shower (1 oz per day). Right after each shower, Adonis secretly pours 0.5 oz of hot sauce into the shampoo bottle; he never adds water or removes anything else. He repeats this for 4 consecutive days. The hot sauce comes from a 16 oz bottle, the bathroom stays at 72°F, and his dad also uses 0.5 oz of conditioner from a separate bottle each day. After 4 days, what percentage of the liquid in the shampoo bottle is hot sauce?
Joanna has $12. Compared to her money, her brother has thrice as much while her sister has only half as much. How much money do the three of them have altogether?

Maya takes a trip to a lakeshore. The drive is 2 hours each way. She stays at the lake for a duration equal to 2.5 times her total driving time. How many hours does the entire outing last, from when she leaves home until she returns?

Jake plans a beach day. The drive from his home to the beach takes 2 hours each way. He brings 3 towels, spends $12 on parking, and the temperature is 82°F. While at the beach, he takes 20 photos and drinks 2 bottles of water. He spends time at the beach equal to 2.5 times his total driving time. How many hours does the entire trip take, including driving and beach time?

Jim had 365 trading cards. He gives 8 sets of cards to his brother, 5 sets of cards to his sister, and 2 sets of cards to his friend. He then donates 18 individual cards to a local charity. After these giveaways, he decides to give half of his remaining cards to his cousin, and later he gifts 12 more individual cards to his neighbor. If 1 set has 13 trading cards, how many cards did Jim give away in total?

Jim owns 365 trading cards and also keeps 12 limited-edition cards in a separate sleeve that he won’t give away. He bundles the regular cards into sets of 13 cards each. For a family giveaway, he plans to hand out 8 sets to his brother, 5 sets to his sister, and 2 sets to a friend. Each set is wrapped with two stickers and labeled with the date, and his empty storage boxes can hold exactly 52 cards each. How many cards did he give away in total?
A vampire drains four people a week. His best friend is a werewolf who eats seven people a week, but only fresh ones, never drained ones. How many weeks will a village of 77 people last them both?

A library has a backlog of 72 unread books. Reader A finishes 3 books each week. Reader B finishes 5 books each week, but always chooses books that Reader A hasn’t read yet and never duplicates A’s work. After how many weeks will all 72 books be read?

Lucas wants to get a dog, but his parents think he already has too many pets and won't have enough space. He already has 12 pet beds in his room and manages to fit another 8 pet beds. Later, he donates 4 beds to an animal shelter. For his birthday, his aunt gives him 3 packs of 2 pet beds each. After rearranging his room, he buys additional beds equal to half the number of beds he has at that moment. Unfortunately, 3 of the beds he owns turn out to be torn and unusable. His parents argue that each pet needs 2 beds to feel comfortable. According to his parents’ argument, how many pets does Lucas have enough room for?

To raise money, a school is selling ice-pops for $1.60. It costs 80 cents to make each pop, and the money from the pops will be used to buy pencils, which cost $2.20 each. How many pops must be sold to buy 120 pencils?

Paul is working at a university. He is part of a big project, which involves 90 scientists in total. Half of them are from Europe and one-fifth are from Canada. The rest are from the USA. How many scientists in this project are from the USA?
Randy feeds his pigs 10.0 pounds of feed per pig per day. If Randy has 2 pigs, how many pounds of pig feed will Randy's pigs be fed per 1.0 week?
Tom decided to send his wife 2 dozen roses every day. How many total roses did he send?
Susan has 21 cats and Bob has 3 cats. After she gives some of her cats to Bob, Susan ends up with 14 more cats than Bob. How many cats did Susan give to Bob?

Jenna is planning a road trip. She plans on driving the first 180 miles, and her friend will drive the last 120 miles. They plan on taking 3 20-minute breaks. If Jenna drives 60 miles per hour and her friend drives 30 miles per hour, how many hours will they spend on the road trip?

An organic egg costs 50 cents when bought individually. A tray that holds 30 eggs costs $12. You plan to buy 60 eggs. If you buy them individually, there is a one-time bag fee of 10 cents added to your purchase. If you buy trays, you must buy two trays and you have a coupon that gives $1 off the second tray. How many cents per egg do you save by buying trays instead of individual eggs?

In Everlee's family, there are two adults and four children. In a cookie jar, there are 120 cookies. The adults eat 1/3 of the cookies. After that, a neighbor drops off 24 more cookies and adds them to the jar. The family then sets aside 12 cookies to bring to a friend. The remaining cookies are divided equally among the four children. How many cookies does each child get?

Carlson initially owned 300 square meters of land. He then bought two additional plots costing $8000 and $4000. The land he buys costs $20 per square meter. After these purchases, he sold 50 square meters of the new land at the same price per square meter, and then used all the money from that sale plus an extra $200 to buy more land at $20 per square meter. How big is his land now?

Lionel went to the grocery store and bought 104 boxes of Graham crackers and 150 packets of Oreos. To make an Oreo cheesecake, Lionel needs 2 boxes of Graham crackers and 3 packets of Oreos. After making the maximum number of Oreo cheesecakes he can with the ingredients he bought, how many boxes of Graham crackers would he have left over?
Ivanka wrote a book that took her 13 more months than it took Woody to write a book. Woody spent 11.5 years writing his book. How many months in total did Ivanka and Woody need to write their books?

Sam tutors math at a rate of $10 per hour. In the first month, he earned $200. In the following month, his earnings were $150 more than in the first month. Over these two months combined, how many hours did he tutor?

Laura took sixteen trips to the park. On each trip, she spent 2 hours at the park and an additional 130 minutes walking to and from the park. What percentage of the total time she took for her trips to the park did Laura spend in the park?

Laura took six trips to the park. On each trip, she spent 2 hours in the park and a total of 30 minutes walking to and from the park. In addition, before each trip she spent 10 minutes packing snacks, and after each trip she spent 5 minutes tidying up. On two of the trips, roadwork slowed her down, adding 10 extra minutes to the walking time on those days. On one other trip, she left the park 20 minutes early. Considering all six trips, what percentage of her total trip-related time (park time + walking time + packing + tidying) did Laura spend actually in the park?

Ethan is reading a sci-fi book that has 360 pages. He read 40 pages on Saturday morning and another 10 pages at night. On Sunday morning, he read twice as many pages as he read on Saturday morning, and on Sunday night he read three times as many pages as he read on Saturday night. On Monday during lunch, he read 25 more pages. How many pages does he have left to read?

Angus, Patrick, and Ollie went fishing for trout on Rainbow Lake. Angus caught 14 more fish than Patrick did, but Ollie caught 17 fewer fish than Angus. If Ollie caught 15 fish, how many fish did Patrick catch?

At Wendy’s, a group of five decides to split their order evenly. They bought one taco salad platter for $10, five Dave’s Single burgers at $5 each, four orders of fries priced at $2.50 apiece, and five peach lemonades at $2 each. How much should each person pay?
Ernie's income is 0.8 of what it used to be and Jack's income is now 2.0 times what Ernie used to make. How much do they earn combined if Ernie used to make $6,000.00?
Ernie’s current income is four-fifths of what it used to be, and Jack’s current income is twice what Ernie used to make. If together they now earn $16,800, how much did Ernie used to make?

Seymour runs a plant shop. He has 4 flats of petunias with 8 petunias per flat and 3 flats of roses with 6 roses per flat. If the total amount of fertilizer needed is 314 ounces, how many Venus flytraps does Seymour have?
Terry earns $24 per day and Jordan earns $30 per day. If both work all 7 days in a week, by how many dollars does Jordan’s weekly pay exceed Terry’s?
Violet has 3.0 more than twice as many nails as Tickletoe. If Violet has 27.0 nails, how many nails do they have together?

Every year, five clowns and twenty-five children go on a carousel. This year, the candy seller, at the carousel, had 900 candies. The candy seller then sold 24 candies, to each of the clowns and the children, who attended. How many candies did he have left?

John has to hire a lawyer. He pays $1200 upfront. He then gets charged $90 per hour. The lawyer has to work 48 hours in court time. It takes 1.5 times that long in prep time. His brother pays half the fee. How much did John pay?

John has to hire a lawyer. He pays $1000.00 upfront. He then gets charged $100.00 per hour. The lawyer has to work 50.0 hours in court time. It takes 2.0 times that long in prep time. His brother pays 1/2 the fee. How much did John pay?

Mike began to train to play basketball every day for a tournament. One day he plays a maximum of 2.0 hours. After a week of training, he increased the maximum time to 3.0 hours. How many hours did Mike train during the first two weeks?

Mike began daily basketball training for a tournament. During the first week (7 days), he uses the full daily practice limit of 2 hours. Each day he also does 15 minutes of stretching before and 15 minutes after practice, but stretching is not counted toward practice time. On Wednesday he adds a 20-minute free-throw routine that is included within that day’s practice limit. At the start of the second week, he raises his daily practice limit to 3 hours and again uses the full amount each day for 7 days. He does not skip any days. How many hours did Mike train during the first two weeks?

The novelty shop on the Starship Conundrum sells magazines and chocolates. The cost of 40 chocolate bars is equal to the cost of 80 magazines. If one magazine costs $10, how much does a dozen chocolate bars cost, in dollars?

Jenna is planning an outing that includes a concert ticket and five drink tickets at $7 each. If the concert ticket costs $181 and the total cost of this outing is exactly 10% of her monthly earnings, and she works 30 hours per week for 4 weeks in the month, what is her hourly wage?

Jenna is planning a night out: the concert ticket is $181, and she’ll also buy five drink vouchers at $7 each. She earns $18 per hour and works 30 hours each week. Assuming a 4-week month, what percentage of her monthly pay will this outing cost?

Ken likes to bike when it's raining and can cycle 300 miles in 200 minutes during this time. However, when it's snowing Ken can't stand the cold and can only cycle 100 miles in 200 minutes. If it rains 3 times and snows 4 times in one week, how many miles did Ken reach if he cycles 1 hour a day?

Ken likes to bike when it's raining and can cycle 30 miles in 20 minutes during this time. However, when it's snowing Ken can't stand the cold and can only cycle 10 miles in 20 minutes. How many miles did Ken reach in one week if he cycles 1 hour a day?

A group of 5 children are taken to an amusement park. Only 3 of them were daring enough to get on the Ferris wheel which cost $10/2 per child. Everyone had a go at the merry-go-round (at $3.00 per child). On their way home, they bought 2 cones of ice cream each (each cone cost $8.00). How much did they spend altogether?

On Monday, Cleo and Ignacio put some marbles into a jar. The next day, they took 3/5 of the marbles from the jar and split that amount equally between them. On the third day, Cleo took half of the marbles remaining in the jar. By the end of the third day, Cleo had 15 marbles in total. How many marbles did they place in the jar on Monday?

Sam the butcher made sausage by grinding up 10 pounds of spicy meat mix, loading it into a tube casing, and creating a string of 40 sausage links. Before hanging the string in the cooler, she used an additional 2 pounds of the same mix to make more links of the same size and tied them onto the same string. In the afternoon, a customer bought 6 links. Later that evening, Brandy, Sam’s Golden Retriever, broke into the cooler and ate 12 links. After all this, how many ounces of sausage meat were contained in the remaining links?

At a party, a round cake is cut into 8 equal slices, and each slice contains 347 calories. The cake is 9 inches in diameter and has 12 unlit candles that are not eaten. A rectangular pan of brownies is cut into 6 pieces, and each brownie contains 375 calories. The pan measures 9 by 13 inches and was baked for 35 minutes at 350°F. No toppings like ice cream are served. How many more total calories does the cake have than the entire pan of brownies?

Mr. Cruz went to his doctor to seek advice on the best way to gain weight. His doctor told him to include more proteins in his meals and live a generally healthy lifestyle. After a month of following his doctor's advice, Mr. Cruz gained 20 pounds, but his new light cardio routine caused him to lose 5 pounds that same month. In the second month, he gained 30 more pounds from healthy eating, and his cardio led to a 6-pound loss. If he originally weighed 70 pounds, and at the end of the second month he stepped on the scale while wearing 2-pound shoes and holding a 4-pound dumbbell, what number did the scale show?
At a clothing store, Mr. Doré purchases pants for $140, a shirt for $43, and a tie for $15. He pays with a $200 bill. How much change should he receive?

At the start of the school year, a homeroom had 15 boys, and the number of girls was 20% greater than the number of boys. Midyear, transfer students were admitted: they were all girls, so the number of girls became exactly double what it had been at the beginning, while the number of boys did not change. During the same period, the class moved from a room with 24 desks to one with 30 desks, 6 students joined the chess club, and the science lab assigned them 18 graphing calculators for projects. How many students are in the class now?
There are 500 goldfish in the pond. Each goldfish eats 1.75 ounces of food per day. 20.0% of the goldfish need to eat special food that costs $3.50 an ounce. How much does it cost to feed these fish?
There are 50 goldfish in the pond. Each goldfish eats 1.5 ounces of food per day. 1/5 of the goldfish need to eat special food that costs $3.00 an ounce. How much does it cost to feed these fish?
There are 50 goldfish in the pond. Each goldfish eats 1.5 ounces of food per day. 20% of the goldfish need to eat special food. How much does it cost to feed these fish?

Tom and his friends were filling up water balloons. Tom filled up 3 times as many water balloons as Luke. Luke filled up one fourth as many balloons as Anthony. If Anthony filled up 56 water balloons, how many did Tom fill up?

Karen bakes 50 chocolate chip cookies. She keeps 10 for herself, and she gives 8 to her grandparents. Later that day, she bakes 24 more cookies, eats 6 cookies, and sets aside 14 cookies for her little brother. Her aunt then gives her 12 more chocolate chip cookies to add to the batch. If Karen wants to give everyone in her class cookies, and there are 16 people in her class, how many cookies will each person receive?

In Hawaii, they normally get an average of 2 inches of rain per day over the year. There are 100 days left in the year, and so far they have recorded 430 inches of rain. Forecasts predict that over the next 15 days they will average 2 inches of rain per day, and over the subsequent 15 days they will average 4 inches per day. To still finish the year with the normal annual average, what average rainfall per day will they need over each of the remaining days after those 30 days?

A certain island’s long-term average is 2 inches of rain per day over a 365-day year. With 100 days remaining, the total rainfall so far is 430 inches. What average daily rainfall is required over the remaining days to end the year at the usual average?
Rose bought her mother 15 dozen flowers. 30 of the flowers are daisies. Three-fifths of the remaining flowers are tulips and the rest are sunflowers. How many sunflowers are there?
How much money did you make if you sold 2,200 chocolate cookies at $10 per cookie and 700 vanilla cookies at $20 per cookie?
Martine has 6 more than twice as many peaches as Benjy. Benjy has one-third as many peaches as Gabrielle. If Martine has 22 peaches, how many does Gabrielle have?
Martine has 6 more than twice as many peaches as Benjy. Benjy has one-third as many peaches as Gabrielle. If Gabrielle has 15 peaches, how many does Martine have?

Mitch has saved $20,000 to finance his boating hobby. He must keep $500 for license and registration, and three times that amount for docking fees. If he wants to buy a 12-foot boat and the price is the same per foot of length, what is the maximum price per foot he can afford?

A judge oversaw court cases. Two were immediately dismissed from court. Two-thirds of the remaining cases were ruled innocent, one ruling was delayed until a later date, and the rest were judged guilty. On how many cases did the judge rule guilty?

Ryan works in an office where the number of men on-site equals the number of women on-site. One morning, a 45-minute meeting is held in a conference room that seats 20 people. The meeting pulls 4 men and 6 women off the office floor. Two remote contractors join the meeting by video but are not on-site employees. Because of this meeting, the number of women remaining on the office floor temporarily drops by 20%. The office also has 12 departments and 8 coffee mugs in the break room. How many people work on-site at Ryan’s office?

At a party for students, each attendee is either a poet, a singer, or a tree hugger. Initially, there are 360 students at the party. Then, 40 more singers arrive and no one leaves. After the arrivals, there are 50 more poets than tree huggers, and the number of tree huggers is 120. How many singers are at the party after the arrivals?

Pulsar, the shuffle-dancing bear, Polly, the pink prancing poodle, and Petra, the proud portly pachyderm, are entertainers at the Big Top Circus. In one show, Pulsar stands on his two back legs. Then, Polly stands on her back legs for three times as long as Pulsar. And then, finally, Petra stands of his back legs for one-sixth as long as Polly. What is the combined length of time, in minutes, that the three entertainers stand on their back legs?

Buffy has a sailboat with a planing hull that she sails in the Gulf of Mexico. Under optimal wind conditions, the use of two sails brings the ship to the speed of 50.0 knots, whereas under the same conditions, the use of one sail brings her ship to the speed of 25.0 knots. A knot is a nautical term for speed equal to 1.0 nautical mile per hour, and 1.0 nautical mile equals 23/20 land miles. If she travels in her sailboat under optimal wind conditions for 4.0 hours with one sail and then for another 4.0 hours with two sails, what is the total distance, in land miles, that she will travel?

Annie goes to school. Today is her birthday, so she decided to buy some sweets for her classmates. Each classmate got 2 candies, and after handing them out Annie had 12 candies left. Annie spent $8 on the candies, and one candy costs $0.10. How many people are in Annie’s class in total?
Solomon collected 3.0 times as many cans as Juwan. Levi collected 1/2 of what Juwan collected. Solomon collected 66.0 cans. How many cans did the boys collect in all?
Andrew eats 18 donuts on Monday, and half as many on Tuesday. On Wednesday Andrew eats 4 times as many as he did on Monday. How many donuts did Andrew eat total in the three days?

Andrew eats 14 donuts on Monday. On Tuesday, he eats half as many as on Monday. On Wednesday, he eats four times as many as on Tuesday. On Thursday, he eats twice the difference between his Wednesday and Tuesday amounts. How many donuts did Andrew eat in total from Monday through Thursday?
Michael buys his suit for $4,300 and shoes for $1,900. So, if he gets a $1,000 discount, what was the amount that he paid to the seller?

A farmer gets 20 pounds of bacon on average from a pig. He sells the bacon at the monthly farmer’s market. This month’s pig is a runt that grew to only half the size of the average pig. How many dollars will the farmer make from the pig’s bacon?
Pierre decides to bring his mother out for ice cream. His treat. Each scoop is $2.00. If he gets 3 scoops and his mom gets 4.0, what is the total bill?
At an ice cream shop, each scoop costs $2. Alex buys 3 scoops for himself and 4 scoops for his mom. What is the total amount he has to pay?

Grant has worked as a freelance math worker for the last three months. The first month he made $350. The second month he made $50 more than double what he made in the first month. The third month he earned four times the sum of the first two months. In addition, he paid a $20 platform fee each month, received a one-time $140 tip at the end of the second month, and issued a $60 refund to a client in the third month. After accounting for the fees, the tip, and the refund, how much did Grant make in total over the three months?

Jessica is making an apple pie. She knows that each serving requires 1.50 apples and she has 120 guests. She plans to make 30 pies, which each contain 80 servings. If her guests finish all the pie, on average, how many apples does each guest eat?

Jessica is hosting a neighborhood dinner and plans to bake apple pies. Each serving of pie requires 1.5 apples. She invites 12 guests. She will bake 3 pies, each cut into 8 equal servings. She bought 45 apples at the market and will set aside 9 of them to make applesauce tomorrow. She also plans to add 2 cups of sugar per pie and serve one scoop of ice cream with each slice; her oven bakes one pie in 45 minutes after a 15-minute preheat. If the guests finish all the pie, on average, how many apples does each guest eat?

Five years from now, Ahmed will be 16 years old, and Fouad is 15 years older than Ahmed. In how many years from now will Fouad’s age be double Ahmed’s current age? Also, what will be the sum of their ages at that time?

Alex is working on a science project and uses a computer program that can automatically identify the plant in each photo. She has 960 pictures and wants them all processed within 32 hours. If the program takes the same amount of time for each picture, how many minutes should it take per picture to finish in time?

Alex has organized her 960 plant photos into 12 folders with 80 photos in each. She plans to use a computer program that identifies the plant in each photo and counts them. The program processes exactly one photo at a time and takes 2 minutes per photo; this 2-minute time already includes saving results, logging, and a 10-second metadata check. The laptop will remain plugged in the whole time, and although Alex considered compressing the images to reduce file size by 25%, that does not affect processing speed. If she runs the program straight through on all the photos, how many hours will it take to process them all?

Jackson is making pancakes with three ingredients: flour, milk and eggs. 20% of the bottles of milk are spoiled and the rest are fresh. 1/4 of the cannisters of flour have weevils in them. If Jackson picks a bottle of milk, an egg and a canister of flour at random, what are the odds all three ingredients will be good?

The building has 36 storage units that are a total of 6300 square feet. Eighteen of the units are 10 by 5 feet each. If the remaining units are all the same size, what is the area, in square feet, for one of the remaining units?

Later, she wins a $40 side pot that is split evenly among 4 players, including her. Feeling confident, she buys back into a high-stakes round 3 times at $15 each. She then borrows $40 to keep playing. In the end, she loses everything she has on the table and also ends up owing her friends an additional $50. How much money did Diane lose in all?

Diane is playing poker with her friends. She starts with $100 and, after an early streak of 5 winning hands, has increased her bankroll by some amount. Later she bets bigger, loses everything, and ends the night $50 in debt to her friends. In total, Diane’s net loss for the night is $215. How much money did she win during those 5 hands?

Diane sits down at a no‑limit Texas Hold’em home game with 4 friends and buys in for $100 in chips. Over the first 20 hands, she wins 5 pots for a combined net profit of $65, bringing her stack to $165. A party has 141 gold balloons, and the number of silver balloons is double that amount. If 150 black balloons are also included, how many balloons are there altogether?
There are gold balloons and twice as many silver balloons. If the gold and silver balloons were added to 150 black balloons, how many balloons are there in total?

Lisa bought a new iPhone for $10,000. She bought a phone contract that costs $1,200/month, a case that costs 20% of the cost of the phone, and headphones that cost half as much as the case. How much will Lisa spend on her phone in the first year?

Lisa bought a new iPhone for $1000 and chose a phone plan that costs $200 per month. The carrier waives the $35 activation fee and includes an extra 2 GB of data at no additional charge. She purchases a case priced at 20% of the phone’s cost and headphones that cost half as much as the case. She also gets a free 12-month cloud storage trial valued at $5 per month and a complimentary screen protector normally priced at $25. Assume there’s a tax-free holiday on electronics when she buys the phone, and any autopay discount of $10 per month only starts after month 13. How much will Lisa spend on her phone in the first year?
A big box store sees 175 people enter their store every hour. During the holiday season, how many customers will this big box store see in 8 hours?

An overseas order travels by cargo ship from Busan to Los Angeles, a sea journey of 21 days. Once the vessel docks, import clearance and inspections require 4 additional days. The final trucking leg from the port to your countryside warehouse reliably takes 7 days. If the warehouse expects the delivery 2 days from now, how many days before today should the ship have departed?

A cargo ship moving from Shanghai to Vancouver navigates for 21 days before reaching port. Customs and regulatory processes in Vancouver take some time. Finally, moving the cargo from the port to your rural warehouse takes some time and it always arrives on the seventh day. How many days ago should the ship have departed if your warehouse is expecting the shipment 2 days from today?

Sofia and her mother go to the grocery store to buy 10 kg of oranges for the week. While they are there, Sofia’s father calls and asks them to add 5 kg more because a neighbor needs supplies. They also pick up 3 kg of bananas and a 2-liter bottle of milk, and the store is running a discount that applies only to apples. When they get home, they estimate that for the next two weeks they will need to buy twice as many oranges each week as they did in the first week to have enough. After the three weeks, what is the total quantity of oranges they will have bought?

Karen is a dog groomer. Rottweilers take 20 minutes to groom, border collies take 10 minutes, and chihuahuas take 45 minutes. On a certain day she must groom 6 rottweilers, 9 border collies, and 1 chihuahua. In addition, she spends 2 minutes to check in each dog and 3 minutes to clean her station after each dog. One of the rottweilers needs an extra rinse that takes half of a rottweiler’s base grooming time. How many minutes will it take Karen to finish all the grooming, including check-ins, cleanup, and the extra rinse?

Karen is a dog groomer. Rottweilers take 20 minutes to groom, border collies take 10 minutes to groom, and chihuahuas take 45 minutes to groom because they ferociously resist. She spent a total of 255 minutes grooming 6 Rottweilers, 9 border collies, and some chihuahuas. How many chihuahuas did she groom?

Karen is a dog groomer. Rottweilers take 20 minutes to groom, border collies take 10 minutes to groom, and chihuahuas ferociously resist. How many minutes will it take Karen to groom 6 Rottweilers, 9 border collies and 1 chihuahua?

An eagle can fly 15 miles per hour; a falcon can fly 46 miles per hour; a pelican can fly 33 miles per hour; a hummingbird can fly 30 miles per hour. First, each bird flew for 2 hours at its usual speed. After a 15-minute rest, each bird flew for 1 more hour at a speed 5 miles per hour less than its usual speed. Finally, each bird flew for another 30 minutes at half of its usual speed. How many miles in total did the birds fly?

At a wildlife center’s flying exhibition, four birds each wear a 5-gram tracker that doesn’t affect their speeds and fly back and forth along a straight 10-mile course. A light breeze shifts direction every 15 minutes, but over the whole event it averages out so that each bird’s effective ground speed equals its usual speed: the eagle flies 15 miles per hour, the falcon 46 miles per hour, the pelican 33 miles per hour, and the hummingbird 30 miles per hour. If each bird flies continuously for exactly 2 hours, how many miles in total do the four birds cover?
Nick is 13.0 years old. His sister is 6.0 years older and their brother is 0.5 of their combined age. How old would their brother be in 5.0 years?
Nick’s sister is 6 years older, and their brother is half their combined age. How old would their brother be in 5 years?

Morgan stops by a drive-thru at 1:30 p.m., where the posted prices already include sales tax. There’s a promotion for two hot dogs for $5 that he doesn’t order, and a $5-off coupon that only applies to purchases of $15 or more, which his order does not qualify for. The cashier also asks if he’d like to round up $0.50 for charity, but he declines. Morgan orders a hamburger for $4, onion rings for $2, and a smoothie for $3. If he pays with a $20 bill, how much change does he receive?

Jill runs a business breeding llamas. Nine of her llamas got pregnant with 1 calf, and 5 of them got pregnant with twins. After they give birth, Jill traded some of the calves for 2 new adult llamas. Then she sells 1/3 of her herd at the market. How many total llamas (calves and adults) does Jill have now?

Nina wants to buy a new video game with her allowance money. The game cost 50 dollars. Nina also has learned that there is a 10 percent sales tax. She thinks she can save half of her weekly allowance. How many weeks will it take for Nina to be able to buy the new video game with her savings?
Janice sees that five juices cost $10 in total, and that buying one sandwich together with one juice costs $5. How much would she need to pay if she bought two sandwiches?

Jordan and two friends went to a café. Each person ordered a $10 meal, and afterward each got one scoop of the same ice cream. If Jordan’s $45 was enough to pay for the whole bill, how much did one scoop of ice cream cost?

Elisa and her two friends went out to dinner. Afterwards, they each had a scoop of the same kind of ice cream. If the $45 Elisa had was enough to pay for everything, what was the cost of a scoop of ice cream?

A regulation hoop is 10 feet off the ground, and dunking typically requires getting your fingertips 6 inches above the rim. A player who stands 6 feet tall can extend their reach 22 inches beyond the top of their head when fully stretched. How many inches of vertical jump are needed for this player to reach 6 inches above the rim?

On a regulation court, the rim is mounted 10 feet above the floor on a 72-by-42-inch backboard; the rim diameter is 18 inches and the net hangs 15 inches below it. A men’s basketball has a circumference of 29.5 inches and weighs about 22 ounces, and the gym is kept at 72°F with 40% humidity. Coaches generally say a player must be able to reach 6 inches above the rim to dunk. A particular player is 6 feet tall and, with arms fully extended, can reach 22 inches above the top of their head. Ignoring ball size, net length, and environmental conditions, how high must this player jump to be able to reach 6 inches above the rim and dunk?

Elsa started the day with 40 marbles. At breakfast, she lost 3 marbles while playing. At lunchtime, she gave her best friend Susie 5 marbles. In the afternoon, Elsa's mom bought her a new bag with 12 marbles. Later, Susie came back and gave Elsa twice as many marbles as she received at lunch. On her way home, Elsa found 8 marbles under the couch. In the evening, Elsa traded 6 of her marbles for two small packs that each contained 4 marbles. Before bed, Elsa sorted all her marbles into 4 equal piles and gave 1 pile to her brother. How many marbles did Elsa end the day with?

Two trains left the station at the same time, but took different tracks to their destination. One took a track that was 200.0 miles long and it went 50.0 MPH. The other took the other track that was 240.0 miles long and it went 80.0 MPH. How much time did it take them on average? (Round to the nearest integer.)

Toby held a garage sale to raise money to support friends who have lost their jobs. Of all the items that he sold during the garage sale, five of the items together made up 75% of the total amount of sales money he earned. He sold a treadmill for $100, a chest of drawers for half as much as the treadmill, and a television for three times what he earned for selling the treadmill. He also sold a microwave for one quarter of the television’s price, and a set of chairs for the same amount as the microwave. What is the total sum of money, in dollars, that Toby made at the garage sale?

Nigella is a realtor who earns a base salary of $3,000.00 a month plus a 2/100 commission on every house she sells. One month, Nigella sells 3 houses and earns $8,000.00 total. House B costs 3.0 times as much as House A. House C cost twice as much as House A minus $110,000.00. How much did House A cost?

Marisol works as a real estate agent and receives a fixed monthly pay of $3,000 plus a 2% commission on the sale price of each home she sells. In one month, she closed three sales and her total earnings were $8,000. The sale prices were related as follows: House B cost three times the price of House A, and House C cost $110,000 less than twice the price of House A. What was the price of House A?

A rope has a length of 2,000 meters. Stefan cuts the rope into four equal parts, gives his mother half of the cut pieces, and subdivides the remaining pieces into two more equal parts. What's the length of each piece?

A rope has a length of 200.0 meters. Stefan cuts the rope into four equal parts, gives his mother 1/2 of the cut pieces, and subdivides the remaining pieces into two more equal parts. What's the length of each piece?

A mechanic charges $60 an hour to repair a car. He works 8 hours a day for 14 days on the car. On 5 of those days, he stayed 2 extra hours each day. The mechanic also used $2500 in parts, but the customer returned $300 worth of unused parts for a refund. The shop adds a fixed $90 shop fee. If the owner had already paid a $500 deposit, how much does the owner still owe?
A mechanic worked 8 hours a day for 14 days on a car and used $2,500 in parts. The owner’s total bill was $9,220. What hourly rate did the mechanic charge for labor?

Bert has a garden shop. He buys his products in a warehouse and sells them for $100 more in his shop. From each sale, he has to pay 10% of the value in tax. One day a client came to his shop and bought a barrel for $900. How much money did Bert make on this sale?

Bert has a garden shop. He buys his products in a warehouse and sells them for $10.00 more in his shop. From each sale, he has to pay 1/10 of the value in tax. One day a client came to his shop and bought a barrel for $90.00. How Much money did Bert make on this sale?

Bert runs a garden shop. He prices each item at $10 more than what he paid at the warehouse, and he pays a tax equal to 10% of the selling price on each sale. On one barrel sale, his net profit (after tax) was exactly $1. For that sale, how much did the customer pay?
Tom attends a party that collects $2,000.00.  1/2 the school attended and the school had 400 people.  How much would they have made if 300.0 people attended?

Jen and Tyler are gymnasts practicing flips. Jen is practicing the triple-flip while Tyler is practicing the double-flip. Jen did triple-flips during practice. Tyler flipped in the air half the number of times Jen did. How many double-flips did Tyler do?

A local park has 7,000 pigeons that call the park home. Half of the pigeons are black, and 20 percent of the black pigeons are male. How many more black female pigeons are there than black male pigeons?

By the time all 20 of Grant’s baby teeth had come out, he had collected a total of $54 from the tooth fairy. He put each tooth under his pillow except for two: one was dropped on the way home, and another was accidentally swallowed. The tooth fairy left $20 for his very first tooth. Assuming the payment was the same for each tooth after the first that he actually placed under his pillow, how much was the tooth fairy’s payment per tooth for those subsequent teeth?
Sam is twice as old as Sue. Kendra is 3.0 times as old as Sam. If Kendra is currently 36/2 years old, what will be their total age in 3.0 years?

Sam is twice as old as Sue. Kendra is 3 times as old as Sam, and Kendra is currently 18. Two years from now, their grandmother will be 70 years old at that time. What will be the total of the ages of Sam, Sue, Kendra, and their grandmother five years from now?

A case of water contains 24 bottles. A children's camp comprising 4 groups purchased 13 cases for a 3-day camp. The first group has 14 children, the second group has 16 children, the third group has 12 children, and the fourth group has half of the number of the first three groups combined. Each child consumes 3 bottles a day. In addition, there are 8 counselors who each drink 2 bottles per day, and the camp sets aside 15 bottles per day for cooking. Before the camp starts, they find 30 unused bottles in storage. However, 2 of the purchased cases are damaged and each is missing 3 bottles, and during unloading 5 more bottles break. On the morning of day 2, a local store donates 1 full case and 6 extra loose bottles. Given all this, how many more bottles of water does the camp organizer still need to buy to meet the 3-day requirement?
A bear eats up to 84 pounds of food per day to prepare for hibernation. If Victor weighs 126 pounds, how many "Victors" worth of food would a bear eat in 3 weeks?

A bear preparing for hibernation eats up to 90 pounds of food per day. It also drinks 3 gallons of water daily and walks about 12 miles each day, though these don’t affect the food amount. Over a 3-week stretch (assume 7 days per week), it keeps the same eating rate and splits its daily food evenly into 6 meals. If Victor weighs 126 pounds, how many “Victors” worth of food does the bear consume in those 3 weeks?
A 12 m long and 9 m wide rectangular floor is to be covered with a square carpet with 5 m sides. How many square meters of the floor are uncovered?
A rectangular room has a floor measuring 10 m by 8 m. A single square rug with side length 4 m is laid on the floor. How many square meters of the floor remain exposed?

Ivar owns a stable. He recently has 4 horses and each horse consumes 6 liters of water for drinking and 3 liters for bathing per day. If he added 6 horses, how many liters of water does Ivar need for all the horses for 21 days?

Ariana is past due on three bills. The first bill for $225 charges 8% simple interest for each overdue month and it's 3 months overdue. The second bill for $150 charges a flat $35 late fee per month and is 5 months overdue. The last bill is two months late and charges a $45 fee the first month overdue and twice that fee the second month overdue and is for $520. How much does Ariana owe in total?

For an operations manager job at a company, a person with a degree earns three times the amount paid to a diploma holder for the same position. If Jared earned $144,000 in one year after graduating with a degree, what is the monthly salary paid to a diploma certificate holder?

Leo and Agrey went fishing on Saturday from 6 a.m. to noon. Leo used two rods and took a 30-minute break, while Agrey switched lures 5 times and released 7 undersized fish during the morning. By the end of the trip, Agrey had caught 20 more fish than Leo. If Leo caught 40 fish in total (counting all fish landed), how many fish did they catch together?

An archer plans to shoot 200 shots on each of 4 practice days and also 150 shots in a weekend tournament. He recovers 20% of the arrows he shoots, but 10% of those recovered arrows are too damaged to reuse. He needs to buy enough arrows to replace only the arrows that are not recovered in usable condition, and he already has 30 unused arrows at the start of the week that he can use toward this total. Each arrow costs $5.50. His team agrees to pay 70% of the cost of the arrows he buys, and a sponsor gives him a $50 reimbursement toward his own share after the team’s contribution. How much does he spend out of pocket on arrows that week?

An archer needs to practice. He intends to shoot 200 shots 4 days a week. He is able to recover 20% of his arrows. His team agrees to pay for 70% of the cost of his arrows. How much does he spend for arrows a week?
Enrico owns a rooster farm; he sells each rooster. He was able to sell a 30-kilogram rooster and a 40-kilogram rooster—how much money was he able to earn?

Moore's family compared mobile phone plans to get the best deal. At T-Mobile, the family plan costs $50 per month for the first two lines and $16 for each additional line. At M-Mobile, the family plan costs $45 for the first two lines and $14 for each additional line. How much cheaper is the M-Mobile than T-Mobile?
Diane bakes five trays with 22 gingerbreads in each tray and two trays with 28 gingerbreads in each tray. How many gingerbreads does Diane bake?

If there were 200 students who passed an English course three years ago, and in each subsequent year up to the current one the number increased by 50% over the previous year, then this year, after applying the usual 50% increase, only 80% of those students are counted due to a new attendance rule. Afterwards, 40 additional students pass via a make-up exam, and then 12 students withdraw and are removed from the count. How many students are finally recorded as passing the course this year?
This year, 675 students passed an English course. If each year the number of students who pass is 50% higher than the previous year, how many students passed the course three years ago?

Three years ago, 200 students passed an English course. Each year since then, the number of students passing has increased by 50% compared to the previous year. How many students pass the course this year?
Macy has a goal of running a total of 120 miles per week. If she runs 15 miles per day, how many miles does Macy have left to run after 6 days so that she could meet her goal?

Macy has a goal of running a total of 24 miles this week. For the first 4 days, she runs 3 miles each day. On day 5, she runs 4 miles, and on day 6, she runs only 2 miles. After these 6 days, how many miles does Macy still need to run to reach her weekly goal?

Allie, Rob, and Allyn each bought a bowl of grapes. Allie’s bowl contained two more grapes than Rob’s bowl, and Allyn’s bowl contained four more grapes than Allie’s bowl. If the three bowls together contained 83 grapes, how many grapes were in Rob’s bowl?

Allie, Rob, and Allyn each bought a bowl of grapes. Allie's bowl contained two more grapes than Rob's bowl. Allyn's bowl contained four more grapes than Allie's bowl. What is the total combined number of grapes in all three bowls?

Eric decides to go to the park. He runs for 20.0 minutes, then jogs for 10.0 minutes to reach the park. When he returns, he takes a different route home and this takes him 3.0 times as long as his trip there. How long does it take Eric to return home?

Amber has $7 to spend on snacks. The store is running a promotion where orders of $20 or more get a 10% discount, and there’s a limit of 10 bags per customer for any single item. Candy is sold in 12-ounce bags for $1 each (all flavors have the same weight). Chips are sold in 17-ounce bags for $1.40 each; some bags have a raffle sticker that doesn’t affect the price or size. Amber will buy only one type of snack and wants to get the greatest total ounces without exceeding her $7 budget. How many ounces does she get?

Amber is trying to decide if she wants to spend her money on candy or chips. She decides to buy the thing that she can get the most of. The bags of candy cost $1 and contain 12 ounces each. The bags of chips are $1.40 and contain 17 ounces each. How many ounces does she get if she buys the item that gives her the most?

There are 32 students in a statistics course. 25 percent of the class received an A. One-quarter of the remaining students got either a B or C. After this, 6 new students joined the class; none of them received A, B, or C. From the group of students who were not in A, B, or C, one-third later passed a makeup exam and earned a D, and the rest failed. How many students failed?

Harold makes $2500 a month from his job. This month he also earns an overtime bonus equal to one-fifth of his $300 car payment. His rent is $700, his utilities cost half of his car payment, and he spends $50 on groceries. In addition, he pays a phone bill equal to one-third of his utilities and an internet bill that is twice his phone bill. He buys a monthly transit pass that costs one-tenth of his rent but receives a $20 reimbursement from his employer toward that pass. After paying all these expenses, he puts half of the remaining money into a retirement account, and then sets aside one-fourth of what remains after that into an emergency fund. How much money will he have left after both allocations?

Harold earns $2,500 this month. His monthly rent is $775, his car payment is $250, his utilities cost exactly half of his car payment, and he spends $50 on groceries. This month, his $45 gym membership is covered by a gift card, and his employer provides a $100 commuter pass at no cost to him. He also has $300 left over from last month that he’s keeping in a separate savings jar and won’t use. After paying his bills, he wants to put half of the remaining money into a retirement account. How much money will he have left after that?
Percy swims 1 hour before school and 1 after school. He swims 3 hours on the weekend. How many hours of swimming does he do over 4 weeks?

Arnold's collagen powder has 22 grams of protein for every 2 scoops. His protein powder has 24 grams of protein per scoop. And his steak has 60 grams of protein. If he has 1 scoop of collagen powder, 1 scoop of protein powder and his steak, how many grams of protein will he consume?

Arnold’s collagen powder has 18 grams of protein for every 2 scoops. His protein powder has 21 grams of protein per scoop, and his steak has 56 grams of protein. In the morning, he has 1 scoop of collagen powder, 1 scoop of protein powder, and half of his steak. In the evening, he has another 1 scoop of collagen powder, 2 more scoops of protein powder, and the remaining half of the steak. How many grams of protein does he consume in total that day?

Arnold's collagen powder has 18 grams of protein for every 2 scoops. And his steak has 56 grams of protein. If he has 1 scoop of collagen powder, 1 scoop of protein powder and his steak, how many grams of protein will he consume?

John ends up serving on jury duty. Jury selection takes 3 days. The trial itself lasts 4 times as long as jury selection. It is a complicated trial. The number of hours spent in jury deliberation was the equivalent of 8 full days. They spend 16 hours a day in deliberation. How many days does John spend on jury duty?

On the weekend, Tony will walk to the store. On weekdays, he runs to the store. When he walks, he goes 3.5 MPH. When he runs he goes 12.5 MPH. The store is 14 miles away. If he goes on Sunday, Tuesday, and Thursday, what is the average time in minutes that he spends to get to the store?
Jairus and Arniel together read 62 pages of the newspaper. Arniel read 2 more than twice the number of pages Jairus read. How many pages did Jairus read?

A factory uses robots to manufacture batteries. For each battery, a robot spends 6 minutes gathering materials and 9 minutes assembling the battery. At the start of a 5-hour shift, each robot spends 30 minutes calibrating, and during the shift each robot takes one 15-minute break. In addition, once per hour each robot spends 3 minutes updating production logs; these logging periods do not overlap with calibration or the break. If 10 robots are working simultaneously, how many complete batteries can they manufacture during the 5-hour shift?

A factory uses robots to manufacture batteries. Each battery requires 6 minutes for gathering materials and 9 minutes for assembly by a single robot. If the factory manufactured 200 batteries in 5 hours, how many robots were working on batteries at the same time?

A woodworker is crafting enough furniture legs for their projects. They have made a total of 400 furniture legs so far, and this is the exact amount they needed for everything they’re building. If the woodworker is using these legs for their tables and chairs and they have built 64 chairs, how many tables have they made?

A woodworker is crafting enough furniture legs for their projects. They have made a total of 40 furniture legs so far, and this is the exact amount they needed for everything they’re building. If the woodworker is using these legs for their tables and chairs and they have built 4 tables, how many chairs have they made?

On a steady 10-mph breeze day, Omar takes 12 minutes to raise his kite to 240 feet above the ground. His spool holds 1,000 feet of string, and the kite has a 6-foot tail. Jasper’s spool holds 1,200 feet of string, and his kite has a 9-foot tail. Jasper can raise his kite at three times Omar’s rate of ascent. If Jasper raises his kite to a height of 600 feet, how many minutes will it take?

A family buys a 24-pack of 500 mL bottled water for $7.20 and also picks up a 12-pack of sparkling water to save for a picnic next week. Their fridge holds 18 bottles at a time, so they chill 18 and leave 6 in the pantry. On the first day, they drink 1/3 of the 24-pack. On the second day, they drink 1/2 of what remains from that same 24-pack. No one opens the sparkling water. How many bottles from the 24-pack are left after 2 days?

Trisha just got a job offer for an hourly job that pays 15 dollars an hour for 40 hours per week. She has been told to estimate that 20 percent of her pay will be withheld to pay taxes, unemployment insurance, and social security. She works 52 weeks in the year. After the first 26 weeks, she receives a raise of 2 dollars per hour for the remaining 26 weeks. In addition, during 12 of the first 26 weeks (before the raise), she works 5 hours of overtime per week, and overtime is paid at 1.5 times her then-current hourly rate. She also receives a one-time year-end bonus of 300 dollars, subject to the same 20 percent withholding. Assuming she follows this schedule, what is her annual take-home pay?

Nine turtles were basking on a 4-meter-long log in a pond where the water temperature was 22°C and three dragonflies hovered nearby. Moments later, a loud splash lasted 3 seconds, and exactly half of the large group of turtles were frightened and jumped off the log. How many turtles remained on the log?

John averages 1,000 miles of driving each month, though in summer he might drive 1,300 miles and in winter 700, keeping his yearly total at 12,000 miles. His car’s manual recommends an oil change every 3,000 miles or every 3 months, whichever comes first. The shop he uses is closed on Sundays and includes a free tire rotation every 6,000 miles. He also gets one complimentary oil change per calendar year through a rewards program. A standard oil change costs $50 (gas is $3.80/gal and he averages 30 mpg, but fuel costs are unrelated). How much does he pay out of pocket for oil changes in a year?
John needs to get an oil change every 3000 miles. He gets 1 free oil change a year. If an oil change costs $50, how much does he pay a year?

Mr. and Mrs. McPherson have to renew their rent by the end of the year. The annual rent is $1200. Mrs. McPherson agreed to raise 30% of the total due (before subtracting the savings). How much does Mr. McPherson need to raise to complete the payment?

Adam is reorganizing his home library after a shopping trip. His bookcase has 4 shelves that hold an average of 20 books each. He spends 3 minutes dusting each shelf (12 minutes total) and buys two new bookends but leaves them on his desk so they don’t take up any shelf space. Before shopping, he already had 56 books on the bookcase. After adding the new books, the bookcase is completely full, and 2 more books still don’t fit and are left on the desk. How many books did Adam buy on his shopping trip?
Juliet is 13 years older than her sister Maggie but 12 years younger than her elder brother Ralph. If Juliet is 110 years old, what is the sum of Maggie's and Ralph's ages?

Frank went to a shop to buy some food for his breakfast. He bought 10 buns for $0.18 each, two bottles of milk for $2.50 each, and a carton of eggs, which was three times more expensive than one bottle of milk. How much did Frank pay for his breakfast shopping?

Frank went to a shop to buy some food for his breakfast. He bought 10 buns for $1/10 each, two bottles of milk for $2.0 each, and a carton of eggs, which was 3.0 times more expensive than one bottle of milk. How much did Frank pay for his breakfast shopping?

A book costs $14 more than a CD. The CD is 30% cheaper than a $200 album. How much does the book cost?
A book costs $18 and is $4 more than a CD. The CD is 30% cheaper than an album. How much does the album cost?

Thomas is keeping track of the rainfall in May for his science project. On the first day, 26 cm of rain fell. On the second day, 34 cm fell. On the third day, 12 cm less than the second day fell. On the fourth day, twice as much rain fell as on the third day. In a normal year, the total rainfall across the first four days of May is 220 cm. How much less is it raining this year than average?

Thomas is logging rainfall for his science project using a cylindrical rain gauge with a 10 cm diameter. He calibrates the gauge so that 1 cm in the gauge corresponds to 1 cm of rainfall. He also notes the daily high temperatures (22°C, 25°C, and 21°C) and wind speeds (12 km/h, 8 km/h, and 10 km/h), but these observations don’t affect his rainfall totals. On the first day of May, 26 cm of rain fell. On the second day, 34 cm fell. On the third day, the rainfall was exactly 12 cm less than on the second day. In a normal year, the combined rainfall over the first three days of May is 140 cm. Ignoring dew and sprinkler runoff that he records separately, how many centimeters less rain fell this year over those three days compared to the normal-year total?

It’s spring! The gardener at Parc Municipal orders flowers. Each flower costs 2€. His total bill comes to €1,890 after buying 250 tulips and 375 carnations along with some roses. How many roses did he purchase?

It’s spring! The gardener at Parc Municipal is preparing for a festival. He has space for up to 1,000 stems and wants to keep at least €100 of his €2,000 budget for soil. He considers adding 40 sunflowers at €1.80 each but decides not to order them. Delivery is free today and taxes are already included in the unit prices. He ultimately orders 250 tulips, 375 carnations, and 320 roses, with each ordered flower costing €2 per stem. How much does he spend on the flowers?

Bea's mom planted 60 Mahogany and 25 Narra trees on their farm. Due to a typhoon, a total of 7 trees fell. One more Mahogany tree fell than the number of Narra trees that fell. A month after the typhoon, Bea's mom planted twice as much as the number of the Narra and thrice the number of Mahogany trees that fell. How many trees are now on the farm?

Bea’s mom planted 50 Mahogany and 30 Narra trees on their farm. During a typhoon, some trees fell, with one more Mahogany tree falling than Narra. A month later, she planted twice the number of Narra trees that had fallen and three times the number of Mahogany trees that had fallen. If there are now 88 trees on the farm, how many trees fell during the typhoon?
John spent $2040 on a phone at a local store, where the price was 2% higher than the online price. How much did Alan pay for the same phone online?
Twice Angie’s current age, plus 4, is 20. Her friend Ben is 15 years old, and the combined age of Ben and his sister is 27. How old is Angie?
Jemma counted a total of 31 grasshoppers around her African daisy plant. If 7 were on the plant itself, how many baby grasshoppers were hopping in the grass under the plant?

Two companies A and B, are selling bottled milk. Company A sells a big bottle for $3.75 and Company B sells a big bottle for $4.25. Company A was able to sell 360 and company B 320 big bottles of milk. How much more money did one company make from the other?

Teairra has 5.0 shirts and 48/2 pairs of pants in her closet. If 6/2 of Teairra's shirts are plaid and 10/2 of Teairra's pants are purple, how many shirts and pants does Teairra has which are neither plaid nor purple?

Cheyenne is a craftswoman making pots for sale. On a particular week, she made 90 clay pots. However, when she put them in the sun to dry, 1/3 of the pots cracked and could not be sold. How much money did Cheyenne make from selling the remaining items at $45 per clay pot?

Cheyenne is a craftswoman making pots for sale. After putting her weekly batch in the sun to dry, 2/5 of the pots cracked and could not be sold. She sold the remaining pots at $40 each and earned a total of $1,920. How many clay pots did Cheyenne make that week?

Cheyenne is a craftswoman preparing for a weekend market. This week she made 80 clay pots and set them on 4 drying racks with 20 pots on each rack. She also made 12 ceramic mugs to sell next month, so none of the mugs will be sold this week. After drying in the sun, 2/5 of the pots cracked and became unsellable. The remaining pots, regardless of glaze color (she split them evenly between blue and green), are priced at $40 each with no discounts on pots. How much money did Cheyenne make from selling the remaining pots?

Today Geoff bought 2 pairs of sneakers and spent $72 equally between the two. Tomorrow, he's going to spend 3 times as much on sneakers than he did on Monday. Wednesday, he'll spend 6 times as much on sneakers than he did on Monday. How much will Geoff spend on sneakers over these three days?

On Monday, Geoff buys two pairs of sneakers for a total of $60, split evenly at $30 per pair. The store awards 2 reward points per dollar spent, but points can’t be redeemed until next month. He also considers a $12 pack of socks but decides not to buy it, and the store’s 10% off coupon doesn’t apply to sneakers. On Tuesday, he plans to spend four times what he spent on sneakers on Monday, and on Wednesday he plans to spend five times Monday’s sneaker amount. Considering only his spending on sneakers, how much will Geoff spend over these three days?

Sara builds a birdhouse that is 1 foot wide, 3 feet tall and 2 feet deep. Jake builds a birdhouse that is 14 inches wide, 22 inches tall and 20 inches deep. What is the difference in volume between the two birdhouses?

Sara builds a rectangular birdhouse that measures 1 foot wide, 2 feet tall, and 2 feet deep. She uses 30 nails and applies two coats of paint, using 0.25 quart per coat. Jake builds a rectangular birdhouse that measures 16 inches wide, 20 inches tall, and 18 inches deep. He attaches a 3-inch-long perch and uses 18 screws. Assume paint and accessories do not change the dimensions. What is the difference in volume between the two birdhouses?
Frank is 10 years old. Gabriel is 3 years younger than Frank. What is the current total of their ages?

Carrie is trying to sneak some mashed turnips into her kids' mashed potatoes. She knows they didn't notice when she mixed 20 cups of turnips with 50 cups of potatoes. If she has 200 cups of potatoes, how many cups of turnips can she add?

Jordan is observing a lake filled with turtles. Sixty percent of the turtles are female, and the rest are male. Among the male turtles, one out of four has stripes. Of those striped males, 4 are babies, and 60% are adults. How many turtles are in the lake in total?

Lucy made a $15 deposit and then followed by a $4 withdrawal. What is Lucy's bank balance?

A squirrel ended winter with a separate stash of 30 acorns to eat at the start of spring. During winter, it had divided its stash evenly into three piles—one for each month—and after taking the same number from each pile, 60 acorns remained in each winter pile. How many acorns had the squirrel originally stashed before winter began?
A cable plan charges $100 for the first 100 channels and half that amount for the next 100 channels. If Alex and his roommate share the total cost equally, how much does Alex pay?
Zack initially had 65 marbles. After keeping 5 for himself, he distributes the rest equally among his three friends. How many marbles does each friend receive?
If 4 crows eat 24 worms in one hour, how many worms will 7 crows eat in 3 hours?

A charity organization plans to distribute 400 boxes of aid to a flood-affected community. Each box contains $80 worth of food and $165 worth of supplies, and they also spend $5 per box on packing materials. Before packing, they pay a one-time $4,000 permit fee to use a warehouse. For the first 400 boxes only, the supplier offers a $10 discount per box (applied to the combined contents and packing cost). After paying for those 400 boxes and the permit fee, an anonymous donor gives the organization four times the amount of money they have actually spent. Using only the donor’s money, they then pack as many additional boxes as possible at the regular per-box cost (no discount, and no additional permit fee). How many boxes do they pack in total?

A charity organization's goal is to distribute 400 boxes of food to a community that was recently destroyed by a flood. Each box contains $80 worth of food and additional supplies such as toiletries and fresh linens. Then, an anonymous donor gives the organization 4 times the amount of money they had already spent, allowing them to pack many more boxes. How many boxes do they pack in total?

Michael is baking a cake and needs 6 cups of flour. He has an 8 cup bag of flour and realizes it would be faster to measure the flour he doesn't need, take it out of the bag, and then dump the rest of the bag into the bowl. How many scoops should he remove?

Donna is trying to figure out if her truck is over a particular bridge's weight limit. The bridge can hold 20,000 pounds, spans 450 feet, and has a 35 mph speed limit. She’s carrying 20 crates of soda that each weigh 50 pounds (each crate contains 24 cans), 3 dryers that each weigh 3,000 pounds, and twice as much weight in fresh produce as in soda. She also has 8 ratchet straps and 2 moving blankets whose weight is negligible. What is the total weight of Donna’s fully loaded truck?
Marbles are divided between Mario and Manny in the ratio 4:5. If Manny decided to give 2 marbles to his brother, how many marbles does Manny have now?
Bart’s winter plan is to burn 5 pieces of firewood each day from November 1 through February 28 (inclusive). If each tree he chops provides 75 pieces of firewood, how many trees does he need to cut?

Every summer, DeShaun wins his English class’s reading challenge. This summer break lasts 80 days. He reports reading 60 books, with an average length of 320 pages each. He also listened to 5 audiobooks averaging 300 pages, but the teacher doesn’t count audiobooks for the challenge. DeShaun visited the library 12 times and wrote a 1-page summary for each book he finished. The student in second place read 75% as much as DeShaun did. On average, how many pages did the second-place student read per day over the 80-day break?
Ivan has a piggy bank that can hold 1,000 pennies and 500 dimes. How much, in dollars, does Ivan have if he has filled his two piggy banks with those coins?

Bob bought 2 show dogs for $250 each to breed as a side business. The female then had a litter of 6 puppies. Before selling them, he spent $120 on puppy food and $25 per puppy for vaccinations. He lists each puppy for $350, but to attract buyers he gives a $20 discount to the first 3 puppies sold. After all sales, what is his total profit?

Carla went to the zoo and counted 12 zebras in their enclosure. She then visited the camels. Next, she visited the monkeys and counted 4 times the number of monkeys as camels. Finally, she saw some giraffes and counted only 2 giraffes. How many more monkeys than giraffes did Carla see?

Marcus is feeding his turtles, which together weigh 30 pounds. The feeding guideline says to give 1 ounce of food for every half-pound of turtle weight. The food is sold in 15-ounce jars, each costing $2. How much will he need to spend to feed them?

The total cost of staying at High Services Hotel is $55 per night per person. Jenny and three of her friends went to the hotel and stayed for two nights. What's the total amount of money they all paid together?

A local high school has 500 students. Forty percent of the students are juniors, and 70 percent of the juniors are involved in sports.

Jared likes to draw monsters. He drew a monster family portrait. The mom had 2 eyes and the dad had 5. They had 4 kids, each with 3 eyes. How many eyes did the whole family have?

In a certain forest, there are 4 species of trees: oak, pine, spruce, and birch. Spruces make up 10% of all the trees, and pines 13%. There are as many oaks as spruces and pines put together. How many birches are there in the forest?
Tom sold 40% of his games for $240 after their value had tripled from his original purchase price. How much did he initially pay for the games?

Lynne bought 7 books about cats and 2 books about the solar system. She also bought 3 magazines and 4 bookmarks. Each book cost $7, each magazine cost $4, and each bookmark cost $2. At checkout, she used a $5 coupon on her total and paid a $1 reusable bag fee. How much did Lynne pay in all after the coupon and bag fee?

A farm harvests 2,073 tomatoes, 4,112 ears of corn, and 985 onions. By how many does the combined count of tomatoes and corn exceed the number of onions?

Charles bought a pack of 20 drawing papers along with 4 new markers and a $5 frame coupon he didn’t use. Each finished picture takes exactly one sheet from this pack. Today he completed 6 pictures. Yesterday, he drew 6 pictures before going to work and some more after returning home. He also did 3 quick practice sketches in his lined notebook (which did not use any of the drawing papers) and timed himself at 10 minutes per picture today and 15 minutes per picture yesterday. At the end, he still has 2 drawing papers left in the pack. How many pictures did Charles draw after he came back from work yesterday?

Tom was putting hardwood flooring into his living room that measured 16.0' long and 20.0' wide. The flooring comes 10.0 sq ft per box and he has already put down 250.0 sq ft of flooring. How many more boxes does Tom need to complete the job?

To improve his hydration, Liam logs how much water he drinks each day. Yesterday he recorded 48 ounces, which was 4% less than what he drank two days earlier. How many ounces did Liam drink two days earlier?

A company is lining a 960-foot path with a fence. Every 6 feet, a fence pole is placed. The entire path is lined with a fence except for a 48-foot bridge. How many fence poles will be placed along the whole path on both sides?
Ral is twice as old as Suri. In 3 years, Suri will be 16. Both have already celebrated their birthdays this year, and their aunt is 40 years old. What is Ral’s current age?

American carmakers produce 56 500 000 cars each year. Then they distribute it to 5 car suppliers. The first supplier receives 10 000 000 cars. The second supplier receives 5 000 000 cars more while the third car supplier receives the same number as the first and second suppliers combined. The fourth and the fifth supplier receive an equal number of cars. How many cars do the fourth and fifth suppliers each receive?

How many visitors came to the park in total over the two days?

Annie calculated she has three times more toys than Mike, and two less than Tom. How many toys do Annie, Mike, and Tom have in total?

John invites some number of people to a party. Twenty percent of the invitees don’t show up. Of those who do show up, 75% choose steak and the rest choose chicken. If 6 people end up getting chicken, how many people did John invite?

James decides to start making his own coffee. He buys a coffee machine for $200.00 and gets a $20.00 discount. He figures it will cost him $3.00 a day to make his coffee. He previously bought 2.0 coffees a day for $4.00 each. How long until the machine pays for itself?
Sally sews 4 shirts on Monday, 3 shirts on Tuesday, and 2 shirts on Wednesday. Altogether, she needs 45 buttons to complete all the shirts. How many buttons does each shirt have?
Sally sews 4 shirts on Monday, 3 shirts on Tuesday, and 2 shirts on Wednesday. How many buttons does Sally need to sew all the shirts?

Bill is a painter who is hired to paint a client’s house. The house has three bedrooms, and twice as many other rooms as bedrooms. In a car dealership with 750 cars, 60% of the cars are hybrids, and 30% of the hybrids contain only one headlight. How many of the hybrids have full headlights?

Benny gets a new piggy bank at the end of December and moves $7 of his old savings into it. In January he adds $19.
