A grocery store has 4 kinds of jelly. They sell grape jelly twice as much as strawberry jelly, and raspberry jelly twice as much as plum jelly. The raspberry jelly sells a third as much as the grape jelly. If they sold 18 jars of strawberry jelly today, how many jars of plum jelly did they sell?

Maya and Ben are planning a day at the zoo. Admission is $5 per person, and the bus costs $1.50 per person for each one-way ride. They have $40 in total for the trip. After paying for entry and taking the bus to the zoo and back, how much money will they have left for lunch and snacks?

Noah and Ava are planning a Tuesday visit to the zoo, which is 7 miles away. The zoo offers a $12 weekend family pass for two and sells printed maps for $2, but they plan to use the free app instead. Each has a student ID, though discounts apply only to seniors. The bus advertises a $0.50 transfer fee, but their route is direct. Zoo entry tickets are $5 per person. Bus fare is $1.50 per person one way, and they will take the bus both to and from the zoo. They also have a 15% off coupon for souvenirs valid after 3 p.m. If they bring $40 total in cash for the day, how much money do they have left to spend on lunch and snacks?
Troy has saved $50 and plans to sell his old computer for $20. Even after that, he will still be $10 short of the amount needed. What is the price of the new computer he wants to buy?

An angler pulls up a net with three kinds of fish: bass, trout, and bluegill. He counts 32 bass. The trout count is one quarter of the number of bass, and the number of bluegill is twice the number of bass. How many fish are in the net in total?

A fisherman hauls in a net containing only three types of fish: bass, trout, and bluegill. He counts 32 bass. There are one-quarter as many trout as bass, and twice as many bluegill as bass. He also plans to sort the catch evenly into 4 baskets after counting, and notices 5 pieces of driftwood tangled in the net that are not fish. How many fish did he catch in total?

During a hardware store sale, Bob buys a 50-foot coil of rope for $0.80 per foot before 8% sales tax and also gets a free 10-foot bungee cord that he never uses. The rope is rated to hold 300 pounds and has colored bands every 5 feet, which he ignores while measuring. Back home, he uses one-fifth of the 50-foot rope to make a small piece of art. Gnuff charges a flat rate of $20 per tutoring session plus $7 per minute. For this session, a one-time booking fee of $12 was added, and the student used a $8 loyalty coupon that reduced the final bill. If the total amount paid for the session was $150, how many minutes did Gnuff tutor?

James is building an army of Warhammer 40k figurines. It takes him 200 minutes to paint a space marine and 700 minutes to paint a dreadnought. If he paints 60 space marines and 20 dreadnoughts, how long does he spend painting total?

James is building an army of Warhammer 40k figurines. It takes him 20 minutes to paint a space marine and 70 minutes to paint a dreadnought. He plans to paint 6 space marines and 2 dreadnoughts. After painting, he applies a wash that takes 3 minutes per model, and then he bases each model, which takes 2 minutes per space marine and 5 minutes per dreadnought. He also spends 12 minutes setting up at the start and 8 minutes cleaning up at the end. How many total minutes does he spend on the entire process?

James is painting Warhammer 40k models. He spends 20 minutes on each space marine and 70 minutes on each dreadnought. If he completes 6 space marines and 2 dreadnoughts in one session, how many minutes does he spend painting altogether?
Ali and Leila reserve their places for a trip to Egypt. After the discount, their combined cost is $266. If the regular price is $147 per person, what is the discount per person?

Aimee does a poll around her neighborhood and makes sure to get answers from 50% men and 50% women. She finds that 32% of women are in favor of shortening the school day by 30 minutes. 51 women in her poll opposed this idea. How many people did she poll?

While preparing a batch of candy, the mixture starts at 60°F and is heated up to 240°F. After reaching that temperature, it is cooled down to 170°F. The heating rate is 5°F per minute and the cooling rate is 7°F per minute. How many total minutes does the entire heat-and-cool process take?

Andy is making a 2-quart batch of fudge for a bake sale. Ignoring any prep or pouring time, how long will it take (in minutes) from 60 degrees until the fudge is ready at 170 degrees?
Josh’s mom gives him $20 to go shopping at the mall. He buys a hat for $10 and a pencil for $2. After buying some cookies, he has $3 left. If each cookie costs $1.25, how many cookies did Josh buy?
Jack and Jill are friends who borrow from each other often. Last week Jack borrowed $12,000 from Jill, which he promised to pay back with an interest of 10%. How much will Jack pay back?

The library has 9.9 thousand books. Over the summer, they sold some books. If only 4/6 of the books are left, how many did they sell?

Bob is building raised beds for his vegetable garden. Each bed is 2 feet high, 2 feet wide, and 8 feet long. The sides are made from 1-foot-wide planks. He buys his lumber in 8-foot-long boards and will cut some of them for the shorter lengths. If Bob has 50 eight-foot planks, how many complete raised beds can he construct?

In a shopping mall, one T-shirt costs $20 and a pair of pants costs $80. All items receive a 10% discount off the total bill. Eugene buys four T-shirts, three pairs of pants, and two pairs of shoes, and his final amount due after the discount is $558. What is the price of a pair of shoes?

If Eugene buys four T-shirts, three pairs of pants, and two pairs of shoes today, how much does he pay at the register?

A bus has a carrying capacity of 8/10 of a hundred people. At the first pickup point, the number of people who entered the bus was 3/5 of its carrying capacity. If there were 1/2 of a hundred people at the next pick-up point, how many people could not take the bus because it was full?

A bus has 80 seats. At the first stop, passengers amounting to three-fifths of its capacity boarded. When the bus reached the next stop, 50 people were waiting to get on. How many people were unable to board because there were no seats left?

After a 5-minute delay due to traffic (with no one getting on or off), the bus reached the next stop, where 50 people were waiting to board (including 10 children). A school has 10,000 students. Half of the students are girls, the other half are boys. 20% of the girls have dogs at home and 10% of the boys have dogs at home. How many students own dogs?

Gabe has a short playlist of three songs: “The Best Day” (3 minutes), “Raise the Roof” (2 minutes), and “Rap Battle” (3 minutes). His app is set to repeat the playlist at normal speed with shuffle off. He also has two other tracks—“Warm Up” (6 minutes) and “Victory Lap” (5 minutes)—saved on his phone, but they aren’t included in this playlist. A honey vendor sells honey at $5 per pound and requires a minimum pre-tax purchase of $40. There is also a $1 tax for each pound purchased. If Penny’s total bill came to $240, by how many pounds did her order surpass the minimum requirement?

It takes 10 minutes to wash a car, 15 minutes to change oil, and 30 minutes to change a set of tires. Mike worked for a total of 4 hours. If he washed 9 cars and changed the oil on 6 cars, how many sets of tires did he change?
Travis has 10,000 apples and wants to package them into boxes that hold 50 apples each. If he sells each box for $35, what total amount of money will he earn from selling all the boxes?

Woody wants to buy a games console that costs $282. He already has $42 saved and plans to buy the console in exactly 10 weeks. If he receives the same amount of allowance each week and spends none of it, how much must his weekly allowance be to afford the console in 10 weeks?
Woody wants to buy a games console. Woody already has $42 and receives an allowance of $24 every week. How many weeks will it take him to save the money he needs for the game console?

Bogan laid out 10 maggots for her pet beetle. The beetle only ate 1 and Bogan had to throw out the rest. Later that day, she tried feeding again and attempted to give the beetle 10 maggots; the beetle ate 3. If these were the only two feedings, how many maggots did Bogan serve in total?

Bogan keeps her pet beetle in a 10-gallon terrarium maintained at 26°C. In the morning, she laid out 10 maggots on a feeding dish; the beetle ate 1 and she threw away the rest. Between feedings, the heat lamp ran at 40 watts for 2 hours, and she misted the enclosure. That evening, she tried feeding again and the beetle ate 3. Over the whole day, Bogan served 20 maggots in total (counting both feedings). How many maggots did she attempt to feed the beetle the second time?

Randy drew 5 pictures. Peter drew 3 more pictures than Randy. Quincy drew 20 more pictures than Peter. After that, Randy drew 4 more pictures, Peter later drew twice as many pictures as Randy originally drew, and Quincy drew 6 more pictures. Lena drew half as many pictures as Quincy drew in total. How many pictures did Randy, Peter, Quincy, and Lena draw altogether?

Logan makes $65,000.00 a year. He spends $20,000.00 on rent every year, $5,000.00 on groceries every year, and $8,000.00 on gas every year. If he wants to have at least $42,000.00 left, how much more money must he make each year?

Logan makes $65,000 a year. He spends $20,000 on rent every year, $5,000 on groceries every year, and $8,000 on gas every year. If he earns an additional $10,000 per year, how much money will he have left after these expenses each year?

Logan earns $65,000 per year, paid biweekly. He spends $20,000 on rent, $5,000 on groceries, and $8,000 on gas each year. His cell phone costs $1,200 annually, but his employer provides a $1,200 tech stipend that covers it exactly. The apartment’s utilities average $150 per month, but his roommate pays the entire utilities bill. He also receives a $600 tax refund that he uses entirely to pay his $600 vehicle registration. If Logan wants to have at least $42,000 left at the end of the year, how much more money must he make each year?

Out of 96 oranges, half were ripe. Then, 1/4 of the ripe oranges were eaten and 1/8 of the unripe oranges were eaten. After that, 12 of the remaining unripe oranges were sold. Next, 24 new oranges were added to the basket; 3/4 of these new oranges were ripe. Of these 24 new oranges, 1/3 of the ripe ones and 1/6 of the unripe ones were immediately eaten. How many oranges are left uneaten in the basket in total?

A city bus departs the terminal carrying 50 passengers. At the first stop, 15 passengers disembark. At the second stop, 8 get off and 2 new passengers board. At the third stop, 4 more get off while 3 board. How many passengers are on the bus after the third stop?

A factory decides to stop making cars and start making motorcycles instead. When it made cars, per month, it cost $100 for materials, they could make 4 cars, and they sold each car for $50. Now that they make motorcycles it costs $250 for materials, and they sell 8 of them. How much more profit do they make per month selling motorcycles instead of cars?
James and John combine their friends lists. James has 75,000 friends. John has 3 times as many friends as James. They share 25,000 friends. How many people are on the combined list?
Jennifer spends 20 minutes on each of her two long-haired dachshunds every day. Over a 30-day month, how many total hours does she devote to grooming?

Jim opens a bike shop. In a 30-day month, he performs 300 tire repairs, charging $20 each and using $5 in parts per repair. He advertises a 10% student discount on tire repairs, but no students come in this month. He also completes 2 more complex repairs at $300 each, with $50 in parts for each. From the retail area, he earns $2000 in profit this month. As a promotion, he sells 40 water bottles at $5 each, exactly his cost, making no profit on those. He also collects $180 in sales tax on retail sales and remits it to the state. If his rent and other fixed monthly expenses total $4000, what is the shop’s profit for the month?

An office has 90 workers. Two-thirds of them are men and the rest are women. The company hires 10 new employees, all of whom are women. After this, the company hires 12 more employees, and 3/4 of these are women. Later, 8 male employees retire. Finally, 6 employees transfer in from another branch, and exactly half of them are women. What is the total percentage of women in the company now?

Hilary is shucking corn from ears that grew on her farm. She gets 4.0 ears of corn per stalk, and she has 108.0 stalks growing. Half the ears of corn have 500.0 kernels of corn and the other half have 100.0 more. How many kernels of corn does Hilary have to shuck?

Janet takes weekly music lessons for a full year. She pays $40 per hour for 3 hours each week of clarinet lessons and $28 per hour for 5 hours each week of piano lessons. Although both studios close for 2 holiday weeks, her teachers offer make-up sessions so she still completes and pays for 52 weeks of lessons. Each studio lists a $50 registration fee that is fully waived by a new-student promotion, and Janet also purchases a $60 music stand she uses for both instruments. How much more does she spend on piano lessons than on clarinet lessons over the year?

Very early this morning, Elise left home in a cab headed for the hospital. Fortunately, the roads were clear, and the cab company only charged her a base price and $4 for every mile she traveled. If Elise paid a total of $23, how far is the hospital from her house?

Josh is saving up for a box of cookies. To raise the money, he is going to make bracelets and sell them. It costs $1.00 for supplies for each bracelet and he sells each one for $1.50. If he makes 12 bracelets and after buying the cookies still has $3.00, how much did the box of cookies cost?

Elena wants to buy a board game. To fund it, she makes and sells handmade bookmarks. Each bookmark costs $1 in materials and sells for $1.50. After producing and selling 12 bookmarks, she purchases the board game and still has $3 left. How much did the board game cost?

Colin can skip at eight times the speed that Brandon can. Brandon can skip at one-fourth the speed that Tony can. And Tony can skip at three times the speed that Bruce can. At what speed, in miles per hour, can Colin skip if Bruce skips at 1 mile per hour?

Colin can skip at 6.0 times the speed that Brandon can. Brandon can skip at 1/3 the speed that Tony can. And Tony can skip at 2.0 times the speed that Bruce can. At what speed, in miles per hour, can Colin skip if Bruce skips at 1.0 mile per hour?

Colin skips six times as fast as Brandon. Brandon skips at one-third of Tony’s speed, and Tony skips twice as fast as Bruce. If Colin’s skipping speed is 4 miles per hour, what is Bruce’s skipping speed, in miles per hour?

Bruce skips at 1 mile per hour. Tony’s skipping rate is twice Bruce’s. Brandon skips at one-third of Tony’s rate, and Colin skips six times as fast as Brandon. How fast, in miles per hour, does Colin skip?

Roy owns a refrigerated warehouse where he stores produce before selling it at the farmer’s market. The fruits and vegetables he stores are very sensitive to temperature, and he must keep them all cold or they will spoil. One day, the power went out and the air conditioner was turned off for 3.0 hours, during which time the temperature rose by 8.0 degrees per hour. If Roy gets the power back on, it will activate the air conditioner to lower the temperature at the rate of 4.0 degrees F per hour. What is the amount of time, in hours, it will take for the air conditioner to restore the warehouse to 43.0 degrees F?
Anika is currently 30 years old. Maddie is 4/3 times Anika’s age. What will their average age be 15 years from now?
